title: Orthogonal Complement: The Other Direction
topic: The orthogonal complement of a line W through the origin is the perpendicular line W⊥ through the origin. Every vector u in the plane splits uniquely as u = w + w⊥ with w on W and w⊥ on W⊥. Rotate u and the two pieces glide along their respective lines, always meeting at a right angle. The two complementary subspaces span everything between them.

beats.narration: What is left over when you remove a direction from a space?

elements.content: What is left over when you remove a direction?

beats.narration: Fix a line W through the origin. Its orthogonal complement is the perpendicular line through the origin, written W perp. Everything on W perp is at right angles to everything on W.

elements.content: Line W perp through origin, perpendicular to W (teal)
Small right-angle marker at origin between the two lines
Every vector on W⊥ is perpendicular to every vector on W.

beats.narration: Now take any vector u. Drop its shadow onto W and onto W perp. Whatever piece lives on each line, the two pieces add up to u. Spin u around the origin and watch the two shadows glide along their lines, always making a right triangle.

elements.content: u rotating around the origin at radius 2.6, sweeping over ~10s
w = projection of u onto W, drawn from origin along W (amber)
w⊥ = projection of u onto W⊥, drawn from origin along W⊥ (teal)
Dashed parallelogram-rule lines from w and w⊥ to u-tip
Same split for every u — unique decomposition.

beats.narration: Together W and W perp span the whole plane, and the only vector in both is zero. We say the plane is the direct sum of W and W perp.

elements.content: the only shared vector is zero

beats.narration: A subspace and its complement carve the space cleanly in two. Every direction belongs to one side or the other.

elements.content: Carving the space cleanly in two — perpendicular sides.
